clearedSpotChecks.check: A credit word of 2^64 or more for the PoolManager makes every zero crossing SSTORE halt with fatal error invalid storage credits state (accounting.rs u64::from_word). Can an ordinary account put the PoolManager in that state, or set its credit mode or budget, so that its writes fail?
clearedSpotChecks.note: This is the item whose error would freeze every pool on Tempo, so it was checked first. In accounting.rs on tempoxyz/tempo main (fetched this session), sstore_storage_credits reads the word with u64::from_word and maps a failure to fatal_external (line 144). The only persistent write in that file is backend.sstore(STORAGE_CREDITS_ADDRESS, account_slot, U256::from(credit)) with credit a u64 after saturating_add(1) or credit -= 1 under a credit > 0 guard (lines 155-202). Writes to the precompile's own storage skip the hook (line 126). dispatch.rs exposes only balanceOf, modeOf and budgetOf as views and setMode and setBudget as mutations taking msg_sender. In mod.rs, write_mode_with_budget writes credit_state_of(msg_sender) through t_write, which is transient (lines 184-216). StorageCreditDeltas adds with saturating_add on a u64 (line 361). The PoolManager therefore cannot be given another account's mode, budget or an oversized word. eth_getStorageAt of 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 at key 0x00..0033620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029 on rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz returns 0x14, which matches the research file. One link I did not read is the flush apply closure in the DEX code. Its argument is a u64 from a saturating sum, so it cannot pass 2^64 unless the closure itself widens the value.

clearedSpotChecks.check: L-1302: do mined Arc blocks with several PoolManager transactions show any effect a serial replay with transient storage reset per transaction does not reproduce (CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36, Lock.sol:13-25, PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-297)?
clearedSpotChecks.note: Lock.sol:13-25 and CurrencyReserves.sol:17-30 keep the unlock flag and the synced currency and reserves in transient storage, so a carry across transactions would matter. I read arc-replay-publicnode.json and found 0 status differences across 40 blocks. rpc.mainnet.arc.io returns -32601 for eth_simulateV1, and arc-rpc.publicnode.com answers chain id 0x13b2. The replay is weaker evidence than its summary suggests. It ran on PublicNode's v0.8.5 build, not the official v0.8.6-rc1. Call gas was capped for many transactions (23 of 34 in block 33,468,850). Some timestamps were shifted. That leaves the receipts root and gas used validation in arc-reth as the main support for the conclusion, and I did not refetch that source. The conclusion still holds, but its evidence for the official build rests on consensus validation more than on the replay.
